# Import format: unit cards

<!-- Generated by `python manage.py write_import_docs` from backend/apps/imports/columns.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Use this to load the paper "Eagle 1-84" unit cards (or any list of units) into the DMS.

Files:

- [unit-import-template.csv](import/unit-import-template.csv): the empty template (header row only).
- [unit-import-sample.csv](import/unit-import-sample.csv): the same with three filled-in example cards.
- [unit-import.schema.json](import/unit-import.schema.json): JSON Schema for the import API.
- [unit-import-sample.json](import/unit-import-sample.json): an example API request.

The template and sample can also be downloaded in the app: **Imports → Download template**.

## Filling in the spreadsheet

1. Open the template in Excel or Google Sheets. Keep the first row (the column names) as it is.
2. Add **one row per unit card**. Type values as they're written on the card. Leave anything you can't read blank.
3. Every row needs a `unit_serial` (or, for a unit without one, a `stock_number`). That's how the DMS recognises a unit, so importing the same card twice never makes a duplicate.
4. Before typing serial numbers, format the serial columns as **Text**, or Excel may change them (for example `1234E5` or long numbers).
5. If you scanned the cards, put each scan's file name in `source_image_filename` (for example `card-0412.jpg`). Upload the scans together with the CSV and each one is attached to its unit.
6. Save as **CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited)**. In Google Sheets: File → Download → Comma-separated values.

Then in the DMS: **Imports → New import**, choose the CSV (and the scans), and check the preview. Nothing changes until you press **Import**.

## What happens on import

- **New units** are added. The customer is matched by name (ignoring case, punctuation and endings like "Co." or "Inc"). If there's no match, a new customer is added.
- **Units already in the DMS** (same serial) are updated with the card's values, unless you choose "Leave existing units alone". Blank cells never erase anything.
- **Importing the same file again** changes nothing.
- Values that can't be read as a number or date (for example `5 ton` in `capacity_lbs`) are kept, exactly as written, in the unit's notes, and the unit is flagged **Needs review**.
- Every unit added with a warning is flagged **Needs review**. Find them under *Units → filter: Only units that need review*.
- The hour meter becomes a dated reading (the card date, or the import date).
- The owner of a unit already in the DMS is never changed by an import. Use **Change owner** on the unit page.
- **Undo**: on the import's page, *Undo this import* reverses the whole batch. Units that someone edited after the import are left alone and listed.

## Rules

- Up to 5,000 rows and 10 MB per CSV file; up to 2,000 scans (25 MB each) per import.
- Dates: `2024-03-12` or `3/12/2024`.
- Yes/no columns: `yes` / `no` (also `y`, `true`, `x`, `1`).
- Prices are only imported for admin and sales users.
- Attachments: up to 4 per unit (`attachment_1_…` to `attachment_4_…`).
- Several forks: separate with `;`. `1.75 x 4 x 48 STD; 1.75 x 4 x 48 STD` is a pair.
- Column names are not case sensitive. Unknown columns are ignored (and listed in the preview).

## Columns

### Card header

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_name` | text (max 200) | Customer as written on the card. Matched to an existing customer by name; a new customer is added if there's no match. |
| `card_date` | date | Date on the card. 2024-03-12 or 3/12/2024. |
| `mechanic` | text (max 100) | Mechanic as written on the card. |
| `work_order_number` | text (max 40) | Work order number on the card. |
| `condition` | one of: `new`, `used`, `n`, `u` | new or used. Blank means used. |
| `hour_meter` | number | Hour meter reading on the card. Saved as a dated reading (card date, or the import date). |

### Unit

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `unit_make` | text (max 60) | e.g. Hyundai, Doosan. |
| `unit_model` | text (max 80) | e.g. 35LN-9A. |
| `unit_serial` | text (max 80) | Unit serial number. Used to recognise the unit when the same card is imported again. |
| `stock_number` | text (max 40) | Our stock number, if it has one. Used to recognise the unit when there's no serial. |
| `year` | whole number | Model year, e.g. 2019. |
| `fuel_type` | one of: `lpg`, `lp`, `propane`, `gas`, `gasoline`, `diesel`, `dual`, `dual fuel`, `lpg/gas`, `electric`, `battery`, `other` | lpg, gasoline, diesel, dual, electric or other. |
| `capacity_lbs` | whole number | Rated capacity in pounds, e.g. 5000. |

| `engine_model` | text (max 80) | Engine model. |
| `engine_serial` | text (max 80) | Engine serial. |

| `ignition_model` | text (max 80) | Ignition system model. |
| `ignition_serial` | text (max 80) | Ignition system serial. |
| `fuel_system_make` | text (max 60) | Fuel system make. |
| `fuel_system_model` | text (max 80) | Fuel system model. |
| `fuel_system_serial` | text (max 80) | Fuel system serial. |
| `hydraulic_pump_make` | text (max 60) | Hydraulic pump make. |
| `hydraulic_pump_model` | text (max 80) | Hydraulic pump model. |

| `mast_lift_height_in` | whole number | Maximum fork height in inches. |
| `mast_lowered_height_in` | whole number | Lowered (collapsed) height in inches. |
| `lift_cylinder` | text (max 100) | Lift cylinder number, as written. |
| `forks` | text, `;` between sets | Fork dimensions as written, e.g. 1.75 x 4 x 48 STD. Several sets: separate with ; (the same size twice counts as 2). |
| `carriage` | text (max 100) | Carriage, as written. |
| `backrest_height` | text (max 40) | Backrest height, as written. |
| `backrest_width` | text (max 40) | Backrest width, as written. |
| `tilt_forward_deg` | number | Forward tilt in degrees, e.g. 6. |
| `tilt_back_deg` | number | Back tilt in degrees, e.g. 10. |
| `tilt_reference` | text (max 60) | Tilt reference number. |

### Notes

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `special_equipment` | text (max 5000) | Special equipment, as written. |
| `field_modifications` | text (max 5000) | Field modifications, as written. |
| `notes` | text (max 5000) | Any other notes. |

### Stock and pricing

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `owner` | one of: `customer`, `stock`, `our stock`, `dealer`, `mmh` | customer or stock. Blank: customer if customer_name is filled in, otherwise our stock. |
| `stock_status` | one of: `available`, `on hold`, `on_hold`, `hold`, `in prep`, `in_prep`, `prep`, `sold` | For our stock: available, on hold, in prep or sold. |
| `cost` | dollars | What we paid. Admin and sales only; ignored for others. |
| `asking_price` | dollars | Asking price. Admin and sales only. |
| `sale_price` | dollars | Sold for. Admin and sales only. |

### Review and scans

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `needs_review` | yes / no | yes to flag the card for a second look. |
| `review_note` | text (max 300) | Why it needs a second look. |
| `source_image_filename` | text (max 500) | File name of the scanned card uploaded with this import, e.g. card-0412.jpg. Several: separate with ;. |

## Import API (for the scanning app)

The same data can be sent as JSON. An admin creates an API key under **Admin → API keys** (it's shown once). Imports made with a key are recorded as the admin who created it.

```
POST /api/v1/import/v1/units
Authorization: Api-Key mmh_…
Content-Type: application/json
```

The body follows [unit-import.schema.json](import/unit-import.schema.json); see [unit-import-sample.json](import/unit-import-sample.json). Each unit uses the CSV column names as keys. `forks` and `source_image_filename` may be lists.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `units` | 1 to 1,000 unit cards. |
| `dry_run` | `true`: check only and return the report (status 200). Nothing changes. |
| `on_existing` | `update` (default) or `skip` units that are already in the DMS. |
| `skip_invalid` | `true`: import the good rows even if others have errors. Otherwise any error stops the whole batch (status 422) and nothing changes. |
| `reference` | Your own id for the batch, shown in the app. |

Responses:

- `201` imported: the batch with a result per row (`created`, `updated`, `unchanged`, `skipped`, `failed`).
- `202` accepted: a big batch is importing in the background. Check `GET /api/v1/import/v1/batches/{id}`.
- `200` dry run report. `422` rows have errors (see each row's `errors`). `401` bad or revoked key. `429` too many requests (limit: 30 per minute per key).

To include scanned cards: send the units with `dry_run: true`. The batch stays open as a draft. Upload each scan to `POST /api/v1/import/v1/batches/{id}/files` (multipart, field `file`), then import it with `POST /api/v1/import/v1/batches/{id}/apply` (body: `on_existing`, `skip_invalid`).
